title: The Valley of Rapha? A New Suggestion for the Identification of the Rephaim Valley
author: Sabine Kleiman
publisher: Scandinavian Journal of the Old Testament, vol. 39, no. 1
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted peer-reviewed journal article. Project stores its own summary of the argument only; no reproduction of the article's text or maps.
summary: Kleiman challenges the standard identification of the Valley of Rephaim (2 Samuel 5:18-25) with the plain immediately southwest of Jerusalem (the modern Emek Refaim/el-Baqa'), proposing instead that the valley named in this episode lay much farther southwest, near the Elah Valley closer to the Philistine city of Gath -- reviving and defending an alternative 19th-century proposal by explorer Claude Conder, who placed the related site Baal-perazim near the spring 'Ain Faris west of the modern town of Nahalin. Her argument turns on reading the campaign geography (a Philistine force reacting to David's kingship over a united Israel, deployed on ground near their own territory) as fitting a Shephelah/Gath-adjacent location better than a valley already inside Jerusalem's immediate hinterland. This project cites Kleiman as a genuinely contested, named alternative to the rainey-notley-2006-anchored standard identification the valley-of-rephaim LocationEntry otherwise uses -- disclosed as a minority/low-confidence view in that entry's identification.views, not adopted as the project's own reading, and not changing the scene's already-built terrain or the location's plotted coordinates (a geometry change is out of scope for a citation-only pass and is flagged for a later review).
